Title: Twice Baked Potatoes (Stuffed Jacket Potatoes) (RecipeTin Eats)

Items: 100 g streaky bacon, chopped into small batons
75 g mushrooms, finely chopped or sliced
Chives, finely chopped (or extra sliced spring onion)

Instructions: Heat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put a rack on a tray (recommended but not essential).
Wash, scrub and dry 2 potatoes, then prick each potato about 8 times with a fork.
Rub potatoes with 1 1/2 tsp oil, then sprinkle with 1/4 tsp salt.
Bake for about 70–75 minutes, or until a small knife slides in with no resistance.

While potatoes bake, put 100 g bacon in a cold non-stick pan over medium heat. Once the fat starts to melt, turn heat up and cook until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Reserve a bit for garnish.

In the same pan (leave about 1–2 tsp bacon fat; tip out excess if there’s lots), cook 1/2 diced red pepper and 75 g mushrooms over medium-high heat for 5–7 minutes until softened and any liquid has evaporated. Set aside.
Melt 60 g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add 40 ml cream and heat until hot (don’t boil). (Microwave is fine too.)

When potatoes are cool enough to handle, cut each one in half lengthways. Scoop out the potato flesh into a bowl, leaving about a 0.7 cm (1/3 inch) layer of potato on the skins so they hold their shape.
Mash the hot potato flesh until smooth.
Stir in: the hot butter/cream mixture, 2 sliced spring onions, most of the bacon, the cooked red pepper + mushrooms, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix in 50 g shredded cheddar (the mixing portion).
Pile the filling back into the potato skins so it mounds up slightly. Top with the remaining 50 g cheddar.
Bake for 20 minutes (up to 25) until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden.
Serve immediately, topped with sour cream, reserved bacon, and chives (or extra spring onion).
Customizations: Swap cream for sour cream in the filling for a tangier flavour.
Use any good melting cheese (cheddar, gruyère, Swiss, Monterey Jack, Colby).
Add a pinch of smoked paprika to the filling for extra flavour.
OptionalInstructions: If you want the pepper/mushroom pieces less noticeable, chop them very finely before cooking.
If your potatoes are on the smaller side, start checking for doneness at the 60 minute mark.
ServingSuggestions: Serve as a side with steak, roast chicken, or grilled meats.
For a meal, add something fresh like a tomato or cucumber salad.
